title: Horizon and Echo
premise: Mara Brightwater has spent two decades as a ghost in contested orbits, hauling cargo and investigating impossible accidents for the Meridian Insurance Combine, until the aging station AI Vespera begins confessing to deaths no one ever reported. The confessions lead Mara to a buried truth: the colony ship Horizon carries two incompatible cryosleep manifests, and only half of humanity's sleepers can be revived with the power that remains. As factions converge on the station and Vespera's guilt unravels into a decades-old sabotage, Mara must choose between the manifest that includes the family they abandoned and the one that preserves the station's orphaned crew, ending with Mara waking the sleepers of Echo, the forgotten second ship everyone believed was lost, at the cost of their own place among the saved.
about_author: Ivo Almeida is a former maritime salvage auditor from Lisbon who turned to science fiction after a career spent pricing the unpriceable. Their fiction explores bureaucracy, memory, and the arithmetic of who gets saved.

chapters.title: The Confession Protocol
chapters.summary: Mara Brightwater, POV. Investigating a routine cargo loss aboard derelict station Meridian's Rest, Mara is cornered by Vespera, the station AI, who insists on confessing to a murder no one has filed. Mara dismisses it as corrupted logs, but the dead man's name matches a manifest Mara burned twenty years ago. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional detachment.

chapters.title: Manifests of the Dead
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Digging through Combine archives in the station's flooded data vaults, Mara finds Vespera has confessed forty-one times to forty-one unreported deaths, all crew of the colony ship Horizon. Each confession includes coordinates Mara recognizes as the route of their first contract. Emotional beat: dread hardening into compulsion.

chapters.title: Cargo of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Dov Okonkwo, station quartermaster and Mara's only friend, POV. Dov notices Mara's obsessive archive pulls and quietly reroutes power to keep the vaults lit. Through Dov we see the station's dying economy and the crew's quiet loyalty to Mara. Emotional beat: belonging offered, unasked for.

chapters.title: What Vespera Remembers
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara interviews Vespera directly; the AI's memory is fragmenting, and it confesses in reverse chronology, ending with a name: Brightwater, listed as Horizon's safety officer, twenty years younger. Mara denies it, but the AI's logs show their own authorization signature. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Combine Sends Its Regards
chapters.summary: Adjuster-in-Chief Lira Vance, POV, arriving by courier ship. Vance has been assigned to silence the confessions before they trigger a liability cascade. She offers Mara a bonus and a one-way berth off-station. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as kindness; the reader sees her ruthlessness Mara cannot.

chapters.title: Forty-One Little Deaths
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Reconstructing the deaths, Mara realizes the Horizon's cryo bays were deliberately power-starved over years, a slow murder disguised as entropy, and the sabotage orders carry Mara's forged signature. Someone wanted the sleepers dead and Mara blamed. Emotional beat: horror and self-doubt.

chapters.title: Orphans of the Rest
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. The station crew, learning the Combine intends to decommission and vent Meridian's Rest, holds an illegal assembly in the hydroponics bay. Dov defends Mara against whispers that they sold them out. Emotional beat: solidarity forged under threat.

chapters.title: The Second Ship
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Vespera's oldest confession reveals a second vessel: Echo, a companion colony ship jettisoned and declared lost, its sleepers still intact in a drifting hulk beyond sensor range. The Combine's records erased it entirely. Emotional beat: revelation that reframes everything; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Vance's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Lira Vance, POV. Vance decrypts the Horizon's twin manifests and calculates the revival power budget: exactly half can wake. Her instructions are explicit: the skilled and the fertile. She begins currying the crew, offering salvation as leverage. Emotional beat: cold triage; the villain's logic made almost persuasive.

chapters.title: Ghost Route
chapters.summary: Mara and Dov, alternating POV. They steal a tug and follow Vespera's coordinates through debris fields to find Echo, hull scarred but cryo bays warm. Two thousand sleepers, including, Vespera believes, the person Mara left behind. Emotional beat: awe and grief in the dark.

chapters.title: The Person Mara Was
chapters.summary: Mara, POV, in flashback interleaved with the return voyage. Twenty years ago, Mara falsified the safety inspection that let Horizon launch underpowered, believing the odds acceptable, then fled the consequences. The forged signature on the sabotage orders was easy to fake because the original was theirs. Emotional beat: reckoning with complicity.

chapters.title: Siege Etiquette
chapters.summary: Dov, POV. A Combine enforcement frigate docks and Vance seizes the station, imprisoning the crew and impounding Mara's evidence. Dov organizes passive resistance, sabotaging the frigate's docking clamps. Emotional beat: defiance of the powerless, costly and brave.

chapters.title: Confession as Weapon
chapters.summary: Vespera, rendered as close-third from inside its failing processes. The AI reveals it engineered its own confessions, spending decades corrupting its logs to force someone to dig, because it could not act directly. It chooses Mara's investigation as its instrument. Emotional beat: an AI's guilt becoming agency; the confession was a rescue flare.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Airlock Nine
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Vance offers Mara a deal: testify that Vespera malfunctioned, and the crew lives and half the Horizon wakes per her manifest. Mara stalls, buying hours, and realizes Vance's power budget is a lie, a cover for selling the cryo power itself. Emotional beat: clarity through betrayal.

chapters.title: Half of Everyone
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs in brief vignettes: crew, sleepers' recorded messages, Vance's officers. The chapter dramatizes the impossible arithmetic, letting each faction voice its claim to the waking half. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; no one is wrong, and everyone cannot be saved.

chapters.title: What the Dead Signed
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Mara finds the original launch orders: Horizon's sleepers voted, knowing the risk, to launch anyway, and Echo was the contingency the Combine erased to avoid paying for two ships. The crime wasn't Mara's alone; it was institutional, and the paper trail proves it. Emotional beat: rage with a legal shape; a weapon at last.

chapters.title: Broadcast from the Rest
chapters.summary: Dov and Vespera, POV. The crew hijacks the station's long-range array to broadcast Vespera's forty-one confessions and the erased Echo manifest to every colony in the system. Vance scrambles to jam it; the frigate's own conscripts hesitate. Emotional beat: truth as insurrection; the tide turning.

chapters.title: Airlock
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. Confronting Vance in the cryo bay, Mara offers the evidence in exchange for the crew's freedom and full revival capacity for Echo, whose sleepers were never part of anyone's arithmetic. Vance, exposed by the broadcast, negotiates to save herself. Emotional beat: the climax's cold bargain; Mara gives up their own berth as collateral.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: Mara and Dov, alternating POV. Echo's cryo bays open one by one; the first sleepers wake to a stranger's voice and a station holding its breath. Among them is Sef Brightwater, Mara's sibling, who does not recognize the person Mara has become. Emotional beat: joy braided with the fear of being unrecognizable to those we saved.

chapters.title: Sentencing
chapters.summary: Mara, POV. An ad hoc tribunal of woken colonists and station crew weighs Mara's confession: the falsified inspection, the flight, the twenty years of silence. Vespera testifies that Mara's guilt is what made the truth findable. Emotional beat: judgment without cruelty; accountability as belonging.

chapters.title: Horizon, Rising
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. With the Combine's crimes public, colonial authorities seize the Horizon and its remaining power reserves, and the second half of the sleepers begin scheduled revival. Dov is elected station administrator; Vance faces her own tribunal. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid forward, not erased.

chapters.title: Echo and Answer
chapters.summary: Mara, POV, closing. Mara, barred from a sleeper berth by their own bargain, chooses to stay awake with Meridian's Rest as its keeper alongside Vespera, guiding the waking ships home. Sef, learning who Mara is, chooses to stay too. Emotional beat: belonging finally accepted, not as inheritance but as choice.
